web.named_query: ("Paul S. Atkins" OR "Mark T. Uyeda") AI artificial intelligence superintelligence policy statements

summary.text: In March 2025 remarks, Uyeda advocated a technology-neutral regulatory approach and warned against overly prescriptive AI rules that could impede innovation, while saying AI risks depend on the specific technology and use case and should be assessed with data and engagement. He also described AI as having been used in financial products and services for decades and said such tools can enhance trading, investing, decision-making, and operational efficiencies. In 2026 remarks, he discussed machine-readable data and super-intelligence tools, saying super-intelligence may make XBRL more relevant and that automation does not break the chain of accountability. In December 2025 comments on AI disclosure recommendations, he described a materiality-based approach within the existing disclosure framework as pragmatic while cautioning about definitional challenges and potential regulatory overreach.

statements.text: As with other financial innovations, the use of AI also may bring risks and challenges.
